title: IRIS-Harness: Harness-level Recursive Self-Improvement for Image Restoration with Self-Improvement Memory
why: A 7-page technical report in a newly created repo keeps image-restoration backbones frozen and recursively evolves the outer inference harness (pre-processing, backend selection, post-processing, test-time augmentation, and evaluation scheduling) with a structured Self-Improvement Memory adapted from Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (already-collected SIM/CRSI, 2611.18856).
mechanism: Closed Proposer-Selector-Evaluator loop over a discrete peripheral harness: root-cause-driven single-factor (and a few two-factor) edits; SIM records rationale, predicted and observed PSNR/SSIM/color-shift, verdict, and provenance, then prunes known regressions and reuses known improvements across backends; a hard-subset composite score plus full-set rollback decides what is retained.
evaluation_signal: Authors report a two-round loop on four real paired benchmarks (full-set mean). Low-light (Zero-DCE, LOL, 15 pairs): PSNR 14.94 to 18.67 (+3.73 dB) and SSIM 0.653 to 0.702, with color shift 45.64 to 25.84, via post gain 1.35 and gamma 0.7. Dehazing (AOD-Net, 100 pairs): mean PSNR essentially unchanged (-0.01) while SSIM rises 0.897 to 0.909, color shift drops 12.87 to 10.68, and PSNR std shrinks 3.40 to 2.04. Underwater (FUnIE-GAN, 40 EUVP pairs): PSNR +0.77 dB and SSIM +0.051 with horizontal-flip TTA. Denoising (NLM, Kodak24): the baseline is retained when no peripheral edit helps.
evidence_locator: Repo PDF abstract, section 3 (harness components, SIM, closed loop, Eq. 2 guards), section 4.3 / Table 3 and the following result paragraphs; README Main Results table matches the PDF. PDF created 2026-11-21 05:36:53 America/Halifax; no arXiv ID.
